data.name: Chile
data.summary: Chile taxes residents on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 40%, but a foreigner who settles in Chile is taxed only on Chilean-source income for the first three years (LIR art. 3, extendable). Afterwards foreign gains and dividends are ordinary income (top 40%, credit for foreign tax). Gains on Chilean listed shares bear a 10% single tax in 2026 (repealed from 2027 by the reform promulgated on 9 Oct 2026). Inheritance tax is 1%-25% per heir above a 50 UTA exemption for children, but for a foreigner's estate foreign assets count only if acquired with Chilean funds. No wealth tax.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (after the first three years)
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation: Global Complementary Tax (0%-40%) on foreign dividends and most capital gains; 10% single tax on Chilean listed-share gains (2026); partial imputation credit for Chilean dividends; inheritance tax per heir.
regimes.eligibility: Residence: more than 183 days in any 12-month period, or domicile (intent to remain) from arrival (Deloitte 2026; PwC). Applies to foreigners from their fourth year of residence.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are generally ordinary income subject to the Global Complementary Tax (top 40%). Gains on Chilean shares with stock-market presence bear a 10% single tax (Law 21.420, since Sept 2022); a reform promulgated on 9 Oct 2026 (not yet published) repeals this from 1 Jan 2027, making them non-taxable. Gains on Chilean real estate by individuals are exempt up to UF 8,000 lifetime and then taxable at a 10% single tax option or the GCT.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Announced (promulgated 9 Oct 2026, awaiting publication): 10% tax on listed-share gains repealed from 1 Jan 2027.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Top GCT rate 40% (Deloitte 2026: 0%-40%; PwC: maximum raised from 35% to 40% from 2020) for foreign listed shares, unlisted shares and foreign real estate. Chilean listed shares: 10% single tax in 2026. Chilean real estate: 10% single-tax option.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Habitual share trading is business income (first category tax plus final taxes).

dividends.summary: Dividends from Chilean companies are subject to the Global Complementary Tax with a credit for 65% of the 27% corporate tax (partially integrated system), giving about 30.75% personal tax on the cash dividend at the top rate. Foreign dividends are taxed at up to 40% with a credit for foreign taxes.

dividends.withholding_outbound: 35% additional tax on dividends to non-residents with 65% (treaty residents 100%) credit for corporate tax.
dividends.treaty_network: About 35 treaties including Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Spain, Switzerland, UK and the US (in force).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Real property tax (contribuciones) on cadastral value: 1.4% non-rural (residential exempt up to about CLP 58 million) and 1% rural, with a surcharge for high total property holdings (Deloitte 2026).

inheritance.summary: Ley 16.271: progressive tax on each heir's net share, 1% up to 80 UTA rising to 25% above 1,200 UTA (marginal). Spouse, parents and children are exempt on the first 50 UTA of an inheritance (5 UTA for gifts). In the estate of a foreigner, assets abroad are included only if acquired with resources from Chile (art. 1). With UTA = CLP 865,812 (October 2026) the child exemption is CLP 43,290,600.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Brackets are in UTA and move monthly with inflation.

open_questions: Ley 16.271 text on SII is updated to Law 21.210 (2020); later changes (Law 21.420 2022 gift rules) and the temporary 50% gift-tax cut in the 2026 reform are not reflected.
What counts as foreign assets 'acquired with resources from Chile' for a long-resident foreigner (e.g. reinvested gains) is not settled.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts taxed on the same scale; exemption for children only 5 UTA per gift. The reform promulgated on 9 Oct 2026 grants a one-year 50% reduction of gift tax (not yet in force).
inheritance.foreign_assets: Art. 1: assets abroad are included in the inventory; in the estate of a foreigner they are included only if acquired with resources from Chile. Foreign tax paid is creditable. Scored as local_assets_only for a foreign family whose wealth was built abroad.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Tax applies to Chilean estates; SII rulings (Ord. 1619/2013) confirm no tax for a foreign non-resident estate with no Chilean assets.

income.name: Chile

income_tax.summary: Chilean residents pay the progressive Second Category (employment) tax of 0% to 40% on monthly income above CLP 977,940 (annualised from the November 2026 monthly table). Employees contribute 10% pension plus AFP commission, 7% health and unemployment insurance up to 90 UF a month. Honorarios (self-employed) issue invoices with a 15.25% retention and contribute annually on 80% of fees.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Honorarios workers retain 15.25% of each invoice in 2026 (rising 0.75 points a year to 17% in 2028) as an advance of tax and contributions, and settle in the annual Operacion Renta. Contributions are due on 80% of annual fees (partial cover) or 100% (full cover); people issuing under five minimum monthly incomes (CLP 2,767,765) in the previous year, and some older workers, are exempt. The 0.1636 rate is 80% x (10% pension + 7% health + 1.45% AFP commission + 2.00% SIS), using ProVida's published July 2026 commission and SIS for independent affiliates (the highest-commission AFP; cheaper AFPs lower it); occupational-accident cover (ISL) is not added. The cap converts 90 UF a month to gross fees (UF CLP 40,828.47 on 3 July 2026).
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax. Brackets are the November 2026 Second Category monthly table x 12; the monthly thresholds move with the UTM during the year (January exempt limit CLP 941,638.50).

Unemployment insurance has a separate higher cap (PwC page quotes 113.5 UF, an older figure) and the 90 UF pension cap is from a news report, not the Superintendencia.

Self-employed 0.1636 depends on ProVida's commission and SIS figures and the 80% base (Ley 21.133 schedule from the ChileAtiende honorarios sheet, whose PDF text could not be extracted); treat as low confidence.
Cap derived from the 90 UF limit effective 1 Feb 2026 at the 3 July 2026 UF value.
Chile's annual Global Complementario scale (UTA) was not read; the SII November 2026 monthly Second Category table (re-read 2026-10-15) x 12 is used and matches the bracket thresholds.

regimes.name: First three years of residence - only Chilean-source income taxed (art. 3 Ley sobre Impuesto a la Renta)
regimes.description: A foreigner who takes up domicile or residence in Chile is taxed only on Chilean-source income during the first three years from entry; foreign-source income is outside the tax. The Regional Director may extend the period in qualified cases. Art. 10 of the same law makes income from activities carried out in Chile Chilean-source, so a remote worker's fees or salary for work done while living in Chile are not covered.
regimes.duration_note: Three years from entry into Chile; extension possible by the Regional Director in qualified cases (not modelled).

income.residence_routes: Chile has no digital nomad visa. EU, US and many other nationals can stay as tourists for 90 days, extendable by 90, and may work remotely for foreign employers (not for Chilean clients). Longer stays need a residence permit: a rentista visa needs passive income (freelance income does not qualify, per the source), and work for a Chilean employer needs a work visa. Skilled employees of Chilean employers receive a temporary residence tied to a work contract.
open_questions: Rentista income threshold (USD 1,000-1,500 a month) is from a guide and not verified.
No nomad visa found; the art. 3 three-year rule is recorded as the only relevant regime.
2-bedroom rent not found (Cuanto Me Cuesta, Portal Inmobiliario, Toctoc, Expatistan and Global Property Guide gave only 1-bedroom figures or were not reachable).
